title: Unification of Germany
competency: Identify the factors that helped and hindered German unification, list its major events and appreciate the role of its leaders.

keywords.def: The loose union of 39 German states led by Austria, with Prussia second (until 1866).
Ruling by strong government power without the consent of parliament or people.
The union Prussia formed in 1867 with the states that backed it in 1866, without Austria.
The united Germany proclaimed at Versailles on 18 January 1871, with Wilhelm I as Emperor.

ideas.name: The Bund, the obstacles and Bismarck

en.text: In the 1850s Germany was a loose confederation of 39 states, the German Confederation (Bund), led by Austria with Prussia second. Nationalists wanted real unity, encouraged by Italy's success in 1859–61; the obstacles were Austria, the German princes, North–South cultural differences and France. When the Prussian parliament refused taxes for the army reform of William I and Von Roon, the king appointed Otto von Bismarck, who collected the taxes without parliament's consent. German nationalism became authoritarian.

en.text: Bismarck believed Germany could not be united under Prussia without war against Austria and probably France. He kept Russia friendly (both opposed Polish nationalism; Prussia alone backed Russia in the 1863 Polish revolt) and allied with Italy in 1866. Three wars followed: with Austria against Denmark (1864) for Schleswig-Holstein; against Austria (1866), won at Königgrätz, which excluded Austria and created the North German Confederation; and against France (1870–71). On 18 January 1871 Wilhelm I was proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles.

notes.text: p.16: "Shleswig-Holstein" → Schleswig-Holstein; "Koniggratz" → Königgrätz (Sadowa), 3 July 1866. After 1864 Schleswig went to Prussia and Holstein to Austria (1865); Prussia took both only after 1866.

p.16: "The German Confederation was transformed into an Empire" — it was the North German Confederation, joined by the southern states, that became the Empire; the Bund was dissolved in 1866. Proclamation date added: 18 January 1871 (Hall of Mirrors, Versailles).
The book uses both "William I" (p.15) and "Wilhelm I" (p.16) for the same king; the lesson says so.
